items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-118740 affectant Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64 (nuget) (score CVSS 9.1).

Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token.

Announcement for this issue can be found at dotnet/announcements#526

Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route.

Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard.

Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target.

For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5 and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest.

items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-100397 affectant rucio (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

Rucio: Unauthenticated administrator impersonation through SSH challenge tokens

While an SSH challenge token is intended as a short-lived nonce for use in a subsequent SSH key exchange, the function to validate authentication tokens does not differentiate between these and actual authentication tokens.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-100397 affectant rucio (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

Rucio: Unauthenticated administrator impersonation through SSH challenge tokens

While an SSH challenge token is intended as a short-lived nonce for use in a subsequent SSH key exchange, the function to validate authentication tokens does not differentiate between these and actual authentication tokens. Because challenge tokens are generated based on an account name provided via headers without requiring prior authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can request a valid "challenge" token for any account (including administrative ones) and use it to authenticate against other API endpoints.

The vulnerability exists because SSH challenge tokens are stored in the same database table as regular authentication tokens and validate_auth_token in lib/rucio/core/authentication.py accepts these "challenge" tokens. An attacker can obtain a challenge token for an account such as “root” via the REST API and then present it as a valid authentication bearer token:

items.title: CVE-2026-122006 — Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file write and read in image analysis
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-122006 affectant activestorage (rubygems) (score CVSS 9.8).

Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file write and read in image analysis

ImageMagick selects a coder from the content of the file it is given, and some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image itself. Active Storage constrained none of ImageMagick's coders, and the ImageMagick analyzer runs when a file is attached, so an attacker who can upload a crafted file may be able to invoke one.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-122006 affectant activestorage (rubygems) (score CVSS 9.8).

Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file write and read in image analysis

ImageMagick selects a coder from the content of the file it is given, and some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image itself. Active Storage constrained none of ImageMagick's coders, and the ImageMagick analyzer runs when a file is attached, so an attacker who can upload a crafted file may be able to invoke one. Attaching the upload is sufficient; no variant, preview, or analyze call is required. One specific attack chain has been reported to us, but we do not assume it is the only one that exists.

The fixed versions ship an ImageMagick security policy and prepend its directory to MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH through MiniMagick.cli_env , so every ImageMagick process that MiniMagick spawns applies it. The policy denies the MSL scripting coder, the coders that read or delete files other than the image, fetch remote or local references, or display to a screen, every coder backed by Ghostscript together with the gs delegate, and @filename indirection. ImageMagick applies every policy.xml on its search path, so the shipped policy adds to the host's policy rather than replacing it. The policy applies to every ImageMagick command that MiniMagick runs, not only those of Active Storage. See the activestorage CHANGELOG and "ImageMagick Security Policy" in the Active Storage guide.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Osaka, Japan's third-largest city, told its 2.8 million residents to be wary of suspicious emails purporting to come from the local government.

The city of Osaka notified the public that a data breach involving a third-party technology provider exposed more than 1 million email addresses tied to an online administrative services platform.

According to a statement published by the government of Japan’s third-largest city, hackers accessed the Arara email distribution service used by TKC Corporation , the company contracted to maintain the administrative services platform.

Anyone who received an email from the system run by the city between July 2026 and October 31 had their email address leaked, according to the city. They warned the city’s 2.8 million residents to be wary of suspicious emails purporting to come from the city — urging everyone not to open any URLs or attachments.

The city breach came days after the regional government of the Osaka Prefecture announced its own data breach involving the information of food support program participants.

The attack on Arara has had a cascading effect on dozens of large businesses and governments in Japan. The company said a November 2 cyberattack exposed 77 million email addresses from nearly 400 customers, including TKC, gaming giant Sega and others.

Arara noted that hackers used their email distribution service to send millions of malicious emails pretending to be credit card companies and financial institutions.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Open source hacking tool Artex "significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours," the FBI said.

Open-source AI platform Artex is being used prolifically by cybercriminals and nation-states to breach government agencies and dozens of critical sectors worldwide, according to a new FBI advisory.

The FBI released a flash alert on Friday about the tool, which has caused alarm among cybersecurity experts for its ability to take any large language model and turn it into a powerful hacking tool that can “automate multiple phases of cyber intrusions at machine speed, from reconnaissance through data exfiltration.”

“Artex significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours,” the FBI said. “The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale.”

The tool was released in August on GitHub by an account known as "Autumn-27.” The developer of the framework — identified as Chinese cybersecurity engineer Li Puhua — released a statement on GitHub on October 8 saying the tool was abused by malicious actors.

The developer denied any responsibility for crimes committed with it and eventually removed the GitHub repository.

The FBI said on Friday that despite the removal, the framework “continues to proliferate through community forks, localized variations, archived copies, and a commercial version … ensuring continued availability to threat actors.”

In a statement to Recorded Future News, a spokesperson said an investigation into the attack confirmed the stolen data but declined to say what information was obtained by the threat actors.

The University of Texas at Arlington warned students and employees that personal information was stolen by hackers who breached the school’s systems during a cybersecurity incident last month.

In a statement to Recorded Future News, a spokesperson said an investigation into the attack confirmed the stolen data but declined to say what information was obtained by the threat actors.

“We are working to determine whose information may have been involved and the nature and extent of the information accessed. Once we have identified the individuals affected, we will contact them directly with information about what happened, steps they can take to help protect their information, and how the University will support them,” the spokesperson said.

When the attack was initially announced, the university took down MachForms – an online portal used by students and employees for event registration, service requests and surveys.

The spokesperson said MachForms is still offline and the university “continues to monitor for additional impacts to university systems or operations.”

The University of Texas at Arlington is one of the state’s oldest and largest schools, serving more than 41,000 undergraduate and post-graduate students.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par Silicon.fr.

L’essentiel Dotée de 36 millions € sur trois ans, la Réserve européenne de cybersécurité commence à se concrétiser. Piloté par l’ENISA, le dispositif doit permettre aux États membres et aux institutions européennes de mobiliser rapidement des prestataires privés en cas de cyberattaque majeure. Ses premiers déploiements opérationnels révèlent toutefois un dispositif encore en construction, confronté à des difficultés de mise en œuvre. 47 prestataires pour démarrer : ce premier vivier de fournisseurs de services de sécurité managés constitue la base opérationnelle de la réserve. Airbus Protect est le seul représentant français identifié dans cette première sélection. Un périmètre qui s’élargit : plusieurs appels d’offres doivent étendre les capacités disponibles à de nouveaux États membres, aux institutions européennes et à certains pays tiers. L’Ukraine a rejoint le dispositif en juin 2026, après la Moldavie. Une première intervention en Moldavie : une équipe a été mobilisée lors des élections législatives de septembre 2025 pour contribuer à la protection des infrastructures et des systèmes institutionnels face à des opérations de déstabilisation hybrides. La préparation prend le pas sur l’urgence : les crédits non utilisés pour répondre aux incidents peuvent être convertis en prestations de préparation. Cette possibilité est devenue la pratique dominante

Signal de veille — The Record.

The New York City government will be able to fine companies $1,000 for each verified instance of surveillance pricing.

The New York City Council has approved a bill barring retailers and other businesses from using surveillance pricing to harness customers’ personal data as a means of charging different people variable amounts for the same product.

The metropolis is the second city in the country to pass legislation banning surveillance pricing, following Seattle, where a similar ban was signed into law last month.

The New York City Council voted 44-5 on Thursday in favor of the bill and Mayor Zohran Mamdani celebrated its passage, telling the media “when corporations use your personal data to decide what you pay, you only stand to lose.”

The bill is a “big deal for a few reasons,” according to Grace Gedye, a Consumer Reports policy analyst who worked on the effort to push it through.

“Once this bill becomes law and goes into effect, it will mean eight million fewer people will have to guess about whether their search history, what they are hovering over online, and more, is shaping the price they see,” Gedye said via email.

“It also means a lot of businesses may need to change their pricing practices — and if they already have to do it for New York City, they may decide to do it for the rest of the country at the same time.”

Signal de veille — Infosecurity Mag.

Turla used compromised Exchange servers to collect NATO and EU-linked emails

Russia-linked threat group Turla has deployed a new toolset called Cereal on compromised government Microsoft Exchange servers, in one case setting it to pick out emails sent to or from NATO and European Union addresses.

ESET has attributed Cereal with high confidence to Turla, also known as Snake and Uroburos, in research published November 10. The group has been active since at least 2004 and is widely assessed to be part of Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB).

The security company identified two national government victims, one in Kazakhstan and one in Romania. It found no external command-and-control (C2) infrastructure: each compromised Exchange server was co-opted to act as the C2 instead.

ESET wrote that the toolset was designed to take commands, run them in memory, map the compromised organization and gather selected messages through a new Exchange email collection module.

Cereal kept its payloads encrypted, received commands as separate .NET assemblies and ran the email collection module inside Exchange's own processes. According to ESET, the toolset paired techniques demanding a deep understanding of Exchange internals with unusual .NET execution methods.

"On a compromised Exchange server, the most interesting activity is not always the message that arrives in a user's inbox," wrote Matias Porolli, the ESET researcher who discovered the threat.

German lawmakers passed legislation Friday allowing the country’s intelligence agencies to hack foreign systems, sabotage adversaries’ supply chains and take down servers run by hostile state-backed hackers.

Intelligence reform is a sensitive subject in Germany, where the shadows cast by both the Gestapo and Stasi remain within living memory. items.detail:
Signal de veille — Silicon.fr.

Microsoft 365 en panne : la France reste touchée

La panne mondiale de Microsoft 365 perturbe toujours Outlook en France, malgré une reprise partielle annoncée par Microsoft.

Microsoft a confirmé une reprise partielle dans certaines régions, mais celle-ci n’est pas encore jugée durable.

L’incident a commencé jeudi, peu avant 19 heures, heure de Paris. En l’espace d’environ une heure, les signalements se sont multipliés dans les Amériques, en Europe, en Asie-Pacifique et en Afrique. Selon Downdetector , la perturbation a été observée dans 74 pays et territoires.

Les services Exchange Online, qui assurent l’hébergement et l’acheminement des e-mails pour de nombreuses organisations, sont au cœur du problème.

En France, les difficultés concernent l’accès à Outlook, la réception et l’envoi de messages, ainsi que la connexion aux services Microsoft 365. La situation reste toutefois moins documentée en volume que celle observée aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en Inde ou dans plusieurs pays d’Asie-Pacifique.

Microsoft ne communique pas, à ce stade, de répartition précise des utilisateurs affectés par pays. Il est donc impossible d’affirmer que la France est l’une des régions les plus touchées.
